hints.title: Permutation Combinatorics by Length
hints.text: Decompose the total count into sums of valid unique-digit numbers of lengths 1, 2, ..., n.

hints.title: Leading Digit Choice Restriction
hints.text: For a k-digit number, the leading digit has 9 choices (1-9). The second digit has 9 choices (including 0), the third has 8, and so forth.

hints.title: Iterative Unique Product Accumulation
hints.text: Initialize count with 10 for length 1. For length k from 2 to min(n, 10), compute product 9 * 9 * 8 * ... * (11 - k) and add to total count.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def countNumbersWithUniqueDigits(self, n: int) -> int:
        if n == 0:
            return 1
        res = 10
        unique_digits = 9
        available = 9
        for _ in range(2, min(n + 1, 11)):
            unique_digits *= available
            res += unique_digits
            available -= 1
        return res
```

variables: n: maximum number of digits (bounded at 10)
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Looping through all 10^n numbers and checking for duplicate digits takes O(10^N) exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Combinatorial formula computes the exact count in at most 10 iterations with O(1) memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that numbers with more than 10 digits cannot have unique digits by pigeonhole principle.
